query: What penalties are typically applied to those performing on public streets illegally?
reference_answer:
Punishment for Unauthorized Street Performances
Unauthorized street performances can result in a fine of up to ₹1,000 under the Tamil Nadu City Police Act. In some cases, performers may also be arrested for causing public nuisance.

Punishment for Unauthorized Street Performances
Unauthorized street performances can result in a fine of up to ₹1,000 under the Tamil Nadu City Police Act. In some cases, performers may also be arrested for causing public nuisance.

[Document 2]
Legal Consequences for Causing Minor Public Disturbances:
Causing minor public disturbances can lead to a fine of up to ₹1,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 1 month under the Tamil Nadu Police Act, 1859.

[Document 3]
Public Obstruction:
Creating public obstruction is punishable under Section 283 of the Indian Penal Code. The penalty can include a fine of up to ₹200 and/or imprisonment for up to 3 months.

[Document 4]
Threatening Public Performers:
Threatening public performers is a punishable offense under the Tamil Nadu Prevention of Harassment of Women Act. It can lead to imprisonment up to 3 years and a fine of up to ₹5,000.

[Document 5]
Penalty for Loitering in Restricted Areas:
Loitering in restricted areas can lead to a fine of up to ₹1,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 1 month under the Tamil Nadu Police Act.
answer: Typically, unauthorized street performers face fines of up to ₹1,000 under the Tamil Nadu City Police Act, and may be arrested for causing public nuisance. They could also face up to ₹1,000 fine and up to 1 month in prison for minor public disturbances. Creating public obstruction leads to a fine of up to ₹200 and/or up to 3 months in prison. Threatening public performers can result in up to 3 years in prison and a fine of up to ₹5,000. Loitering in restricted areas can incur a fine of up to ₹1,000 and up to 1 month in prison.
